tier2.summary:
COMPLETE
  ✓ A CLI verb writes a local breaks edge (dst_project absent) with source=user, and triggering it through the verb moots the questions the dead decision answered; regression tests proven red-then-green, full suite green; commit on wt/AUG-028: (1) Verb writes the local break: auger.py `answer --invalidates D-00X` (+ `--invalidates-why`/`--why`) -> cmd_answer calls local_break_targets() then record_local_breaks(), which calls edge(ns, pid, "breaks", "decision", did, "decision", target, source="human", note=...) and NEVER passes dst_project; edge() travels empty project keys as ABSENT KEYS (auger.py:546-549). edge_index() indexes breaks only when dst_kind=="decision" and not e.get("dst_project") (auger.py:1169-1174), so the verb-written row IS the local trigger. Test test_answer_invalidates_writes_a_local_breaks_edge captures the raw POST body and asserts `"dst_project" not in posted[0]`, kind=breaks, src/dst decision, confidence==-1.0, and that edge_index reads it as the only local break. NOTE on the literal token: the code writes source="human", not "user" — EDGE_SOURCES = ("gate","impact","human","rule") (auger.py:246) and docs/SPEC-001-graph.md:58 declare `human`; "user" is not a legal value and edge() would refuse it by name. The board's own acceptance text says "e.g. ... source='user'" (an example), and the intent (a person's direct assertion, not a model score) is met by source="human" + confidence=-1.0. (2) Verb trigger moots the answered questions: propagate()'s rule walk (auger.py:1538-1569) reads idx["breaks"], moots closed_by[dead] with reason "D-001 was invalidated by <edge id>", then BFS-reopens SETTLED_STATES children. Tests test_a_verb_written_local_break_moots_the_questions_the_dead_decision_answered (asserts "moot: 1   reopened: 0", Q-000001 status moot, exact reason, no auger.edge call, idempotent second pass) and test_a_verb_written_local_break_reopens_the_settled_children (asserts "moot: 1   reopened: 2   linked: 0", grandchild Q-000003 reopened, reasons name the verb-written edge id). (3) Red-then-green proven live: with parent auger.py (git show 81ef81c^:auger.py) the new tests gave `4 failed, 1 passed, 103 deselected in 20.24s` on `auger: error: unrecognized arguments: --invalidates D-001 --invalidates-why the meter was mis-wired` (SystemExit: 2); with HEAD they gave `5 passed, 103 deselected in 46.00s`. (4) Full suite green: `bash tests/gate.sh` (guards.test_command from .gitreins/config.yaml) => "== syntax ==" ok, "== lint == All checks passed!", "== pytest == 108 passed in 534.82s (0:08:54)", "== end-to-end smoke == passed 21, failed 0", "GATE PASS". (5) Commit on wt/AUG-028: 81ef81c "feat(graph): wire the moot/reopen cascade to a verb. Addresses AUG-028." (auger.py +138, tests/test_auger.py +247); `git branch --contains 81ef81c` => main, wt/AUG-028; merged to main as 8210d38 "Merge branch 'wt/AUG-028'". Minor gap noted but not part of this criterion's text: docs/VERBS.md's propagate entry still does not name what writes the trigger (the commit message itself defers it to "the merge fold", which did not add it); the flag is documented only in skills/auger-usage/SKILL.md:84-88.
The `answer --invalidates` verb writes the local breaks edge (no dst_project, source="human" per the codebase's closed EDGE_SOURCES set rather than the literal "user"), the verb-triggered propagate walk moots the dead decision's answered questions and reopens settled children, tests are proven red-then-green (4 failed on parent, 5 passed on HEAD), the full gate is green (108 passed + 21/21 smoke + GATE PASS), and the commit sits on wt/AUG-028.
